title: Report evidence and gaps for repository test layers

fields.outcome: A maintainer can see which test layers have repository evidence, which appear absent, and which are only weakly or nominally represented before deciding how to improve testing.
fields.scope: Extend survey with read-only, stack-aware evidence for unit, component, integration, functional/API, end-to-end, regression, and contract layers. Core owns the generic result contract; optional stack modules own stack-specific signals; a coding agent may ask for and record consumer-reviewed local aliases and layer selections.
fields.acceptance: The report distinguishes evidence from proof, represents an empty-test repository honestly, and does not execute discovered project commands.
fields.decisions: ADR-0013 fixes the portable taxonomy and permits conservative suspected-nominal signals such as empty, skipped-only, assertion-free, or unconditional-success test artifacts. These are warnings with evidence, not semantic judgments.
fields.verification: Use fixtures for no tests, one layer, multiple layers, ambiguous naming, empty or skipped tests, assertion-like and assertion-free files, monorepos, malformed manifests, and paths with spaces.
fields.dependencies: Implemented in the working tree; local organization mappings are consumer-reviewed project configuration.
fields.risks: Static inspection cannot establish behavioral value or executed coverage; overconfident labels would fabricate a baseline.
fields.changes: Implemented additive survey test-layer evidence, portable/local taxonomy mapping, file/script/config/pipeline signals, and conservative suspected-nominal classifications without command execution.
fields.evidence: Workflow fixtures cover no-execution, present/absent layers, nominal files, and local aliases.

criteria.expectation: Survey reports each supported test layer with the scripts, files, configuration, or pipeline references that caused its classification.
Each layer is classified using explicit states that distinguish present evidence, absent evidence, ambiguous evidence, and suspected nominal coverage without claiming semantic adequacy.
A repository with no test evidence reports that state and missing layers without inventing commands, coverage, or a passing baseline.
Survey does not execute package scripts, test binaries, pipeline steps, or commands discovered in repository content.
Stack-specific detection can be supplied by a module without making the core depend on Node, a particular runner, or a hosted service.
A consumer can review and retain organization-specific layer selections and aliases without changing the portable core vocabulary for other repositories.
Existing survey fields remain compatible and the new test-layer section is additive for consumers of schema version 1 output.
